scope: Theorem 3.2 (Inner decoding) of the manuscript “Constant-factor hardness of Min-UnCut” (preprints/Constant-factor-hardness-of-Min-UnCut-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 102 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3300408a7ae8900e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 9-10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: For every rational J ≥ 1, there are effectively selectable integers m, n ≥ 2 and positive rational constants σ, δ, η, p, θ < 1, with η ≤ σ, depending only on J, with the following property. For any finite weighted family of nonempty affine alphabets and folded bit proofs, suppose εj ≤ Jbj (j = 1, 2, 3). 9 Draw ξ, a standard Gaussian c ∈ ℝX, independent uniform x ∈ X and i ∈ [m], and all background rows independently and uniformly in D(Aξ). With probability at least p, the function b 7−→ hx(B[Bi x−i ← b], c) has a Fourier coefficient of absolute value at least θ at an odd frequency of D(Aξ). Equivalently, the event is max α∈D(Aξ)∗:α(1)=1 ⏐ ⏐ ⏐𝔼b∈D(Aξ)hx(B[Bi x−i ← b], c)(−1)α(b) ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ ≥ θ. (3.5) For every folded proof, without any test assumption, one has pointwise ‖h(B, c)‖2,x ≤ σ−1 , |hx(B, c)| ≤ √ N/σ. (3.6)
